review::.::holistic::design_coherence::w.summary: Workflow composables are only superficially separated; `useWorkflowEditor` still owns their real behavior through oversized option bags.

evidence: `useContextMenu.ts` requires a 20-field `UseContextMenuOptions` object covering grouping, layout, clipboard, execution, deletion, and pinning, so the composable is effectively a thin command dispatcher over editor state rather than an independent module.

`useNodeDrag.ts` and `useNodeInteraction.ts` both take broad editor-owned capabilities (`emit`, Vue Flow mutators, grouping preview callbacks, store access, projection functions, sync state), which means callers must know internal collaboration, grouping, and persistence choreography to use them correctly.

`useWorkflowEditor.ts` manually stitches these wide contracts together and also patches cross-composable behavior itself (`handleNodeClick` repairing selection state, pane/drag handlers closing menus, `syncResetRef` coordinating removal resets), showing the responsibility split is not aligned with real ownership.
detail.suggestion: Introduce a narrower workflow-editor domain boundary: extract a shared editor actions/service object for mutation commands and a shared interaction context for graph state, then have UI helpers consume those cohesive interfaces instead of ad hoc callback bags. `useContextMenu`, `useNodeDrag`, and `useNodeInteraction` should depend on stable command groups (selection, clipboard, grouping, execution) rather than on `useWorkflowEditor` assembling every individual function.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::g.summary: Group resizing and `commit_drag_layout` transaction assembly are duplicated across multiple workflow helpers.

evidence: `useNodeDrag.ts`, `useNodeInteraction.ts`, and `useGrouping.ts` each define their own `createTxnId()` and each build `commit_drag_layout` payloads with `groups`, `step_positions`, and `group_id_by_step_id`, but each does so in a different local code path.

All four modules recalculate affected group bounds with `buildGroupBoundsFromPositions(...)` plus local `boundsChanged` / `positionChanged` helpers, even though they are all expressing the same domain rule: recompute group geometry after a workflow structure change.

Because delete, drag, ungroup, and tidy-layout each carry their own geometry/transaction code, any change to group-fit semantics or payload shape now requires synchronized edits across four files instead of one authoritative layout-commit layer.
detail.suggestion: Extract a shared workflow layout transaction module that owns `txn_id` creation, affected-group detection, bounds recomputation, and `commit_drag_layout` payload building. Then have drag, delete, grouping, and layout operations delegate to that module with operation-specific inputs, so group geometry rules live in one place.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: Three modules independently rebuild the same drag-layout commit plan

evidence: `useNodeDrag.handleNodeDragStop` computes membership overrides, affected groups, resized bounds, relative step positions, and a `commit_drag_layout` payload in one branch (`assets/vue/composables/workflow/useNodeDrag.ts:657-814`).

`useGrouping.ungroupSelectedSteps` repeats the same pattern of recomputing affected group bounds, deriving step positions, and emitting `commit_drag_layout` (`assets/vue/composables/workflow/useGrouping.ts:200-344`).
`useNodeInteraction.computeDeleteLayoutCommit` builds another variant of the same payload for delete flows (`assets/vue/composables/workflow/useNodeInteraction.ts:58-157`).

Because `useWorkflowEditor` wires all of these emitters separately (`assets/vue/composables/workflow/useWorkflowEditor.ts:98-140`), any rule change in layout reconciliation now requires synchronized edits across multiple modules.
detail.suggestion: Extract a shared graph-mutation planner that accepts current nodes, pending membership overrides, and affected step/group ids, then returns one canonical `commit_drag_layout` payload plus any optimistic node adjustments. Migrate delete, drag-stop, and ungroup flows to call that planner first, then stage the refactor by 1) introducing the helper under `assets/vue/composables/workflow/graph_mutations/`, 2) switching `useGrouping`, 3) switching `useNodeInteraction`, 4) switching `useNodeDrag`, and 5) validating with `pnpm vitest useWorkflowNodeActions useContextExplorer` plus workflow interaction tests once added.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: Step config dirty tracking loses nested edits because the original snapshot is shallow

evidence: On open, `useStepConfig` records the original config as `originalValues.value = { ...values }` (`assets/vue/components/flow/step_config/useStepConfig.ts:95-102`), which preserves nested object and array references.
On save it repeats the same shallow snapshot (`assets/vue/components/flow/step_config/useStepConfig.ts:158-166`).

Dirty detection later compares `fieldValues` to `originalValues` with `JSON.stringify` (`assets/vue/components/flow/step_config/useStepConfig.ts:55-68`), so in-place mutation of nested values can change both objects together and suppress the close-confirmation path.
The reviewed scope already contains deep-clone and deep-equality helpers (`deps/live_vue/assets/utils.ts:338-385`), so the current contract is shallower than the state being tracked.
detail.suggestion: Snapshot config state with a deep clone on open/save and compare via a structural equality helper rather than serializing field-by-field. The minimal fix is to replace both shallow spreads with a deep clone and use one deep comparator in `hasUnsavedChanges`; then add a regression test that edits a nested JSON/search field in place and expects `hasUnsavedChanges` to become true.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::cont.summary: Context-menu logic conflates unknown node ids with real group nodes

evidence: When `targetType === 'node'`, `useContextMenu` asks only `findStepNodeById`; if that returns null, it unconditionally renders group actions (`assets/vue/composables/workflow/useContextMenu.ts:67-75`).

`handleContextMenuSelect` then forwards `delete-group` and `tidy-group` using the same raw `nodeId` without verifying that the target is actually a group (`assets/vue/composables/workflow/useContextMenu.ts:145-157`).

Upstream, `useNodeInteraction.handleSelectionContextMenu` stores only `targetType: 'node'` and `targetNodeId` in the menu state (`assets/vue/composables/workflow/useNodeInteraction.ts:235-245`), so the menu layer has no reliable way to distinguish a group from a stale id or a future non-step node type.
detail.suggestion: Make node kind explicit in the context-menu contract. Pass `targetNodeKind: 'step' | 'group'` (or the full node type) from `useNodeInteraction`, and have `useContextMenu` branch on that explicit kind instead of failed step lookup. As a guard, make destructive group actions no-op unless the current target still resolves to a group node.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::live_f.summary: `useLiveForm.submit` advertises `Promise<Form<T>>` but can return arbitrary replies or undefined

evidence: The public contract says `submit: () => Promise<Form<T>>` in `UseLiveFormReturn<T>` (`deps/live_vue/assets/useLiveForm.ts:201-210`).
The implementation resolves the raw LiveView callback payload directly (`deps/live_vue/assets/useLiveForm.ts:538-554`), and that payload is not typed as `Form<T>` anywhere.
The no-hook branch returns `Promise.resolve(undefined as any)` (`deps/live_vue/assets/useLiveForm.ts:556-560`), so the declared return type is false on a reachable path.

The underlying hook API is intentionally `Promise<any>` / callback `any` (`deps/phoenix_live_view/assets/js/phoenix_live_view/view_hook.ts:397-417`), which means `useLiveForm` must narrow its own return type instead of re-exporting a stronger promise than it can keep.
detail.suggestion: Either narrow the public signature to the real contract, such as `Promise<Form<T> | undefined | ServerReply>`, or normalize the callback so `submit()` always resolves a concrete `Form<T>` shape. The safer staged fix is 1) introduce a `SubmitResult<T>` type, 2) update `submit` and the injection helpers to return that type, 3) add one test for the LiveView path and one for the no-hook fallback.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::work.summary: Core workflow interaction paths have no direct tests in this batch

evidence: The only assigned test file is `assets/vue/components/flow/step_config/useContextExplorer.test.ts`, and it covers a pure data-shaping path rather than graph mutation behavior.

The highest-risk files in scope are large interaction modules with no assigned companion tests: `useNodeDrag.ts` (857 LOC), `useWorkflowEditor.ts` (567 LOC), `useGrouping.ts` (382 LOC), and `useLayoutEngine.ts` (336 LOC).
The defects found in this review sit in drag-stop reconciliation, grouping, and menu-target seams, exactly the areas not exercised by the existing assigned test.
detail.suggestion: Add seam-focused tests before adding more editor features. Stage the coverage as: 1) unit-test a shared layout-commit planner once extracted, 2) add targeted tests for `useContextMenu` node-kind handling, 3) add grouping/drag-stop tests that assert emitted `commit_drag_layout` payloads, and 4) add one higher-level `useWorkflowEditor` integration test that exercises selection, context menu, and grouping together. Validate with `pnpm vitest assets/vue/composables/workflow assets/vue/components/flow/step_config` after each stage.
